segments.text: On one side, a machine designed at the leading edge embodies every principle of the prevailing International Style. On the other, a handmade production expresses precisely what the Modern spirit opposed. The robot is a complete break from historical continuity: a new invention conceived by a single, formally trained engineer, embracing innovation and refusing boundaries. By contrast, the status-quo factory is scarcely an act of design at all. It is a collection of disparate buildings, tracing back through several generations of engineers without academic training.
